question.text: 'Sahyadri Angels Fund' is a SEBI-registered Angel Fund (sub-category of Cat I AIF) raising capital from HNI angel investors. Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations and the revised 2025 framework, which of the following is TRUE about Angel Funds?

answer.text: Maximum 1,000 angel investors per scheme, same as other Cat I AIFs
Minimum investment from an angel investor is INR 1 crore, same as regular AIFs

Angel Funds raise funds only from Accredited Investors (and KMPs); no minimum value of investment; investment by Angel Fund in an investee company must be between INR 10 lakh and INR 25 crore; lock-in of 1 year (6 months if sold to third party)
Angel Funds can list units on a recognised stock exchange for liquidity

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI (AIF) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2025 on Angel Funds: (i) raise funds only from Accredited Investors + KMPs of fund/manager; (ii) no minimum investment by angel investor; (iii) investment per investee company between INR 10 lakh and INR 25 crore (including follow-ons); (iv) lock-in 1 year, 6 months if exit to third party; (v) at least 2 AIs must contribute to each deal; (vi) Manager/Sponsor continuing interest: 0.5% per investment or INR 50,000, whichever is higher. The Trap: Option A cites wrong investor cap (Angel Fund cap was historically 200, but post-2025 the framework emphasizes AI-only participation). Option B is false — no minimum value for angel investor. Option D is wrong — Angel Fund units cannot be listed. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests Angel-Fund product structure. XIX-C requires the 2025 amendment details (AI-only, 5-AI first close, KMP carve-out). Manager's Pro-Tip: Manager tip: Each investment must have contribution from at least 2 Accredited Investors; investee cannot be promoted by a corporate group with turnover > INR 300 crore. Maintain per-deal term sheets and pro-rata follow-on allocation records — critical for SFA implementation standards audit.
